output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses comes mainly from the 12 August alert relay server hardware move, not from agency staffing. The import skipped 11 of 14 forwarding rules. Those rules held back brief SpO2 alarms, suppressed repeat notifications, and sent technical alarms only to the pod charge phone. Since then, phone notifications per nurse in Pods A–C have roughly doubled and acknowledgement time has doubled. Pod D was not migrated and shows no change. Core, agency and Pod D staff all behave the same way, so this looks like alarm overload, not poor skills. Bedside alarm volume did not change, which rules out acuity and the monitor update. Agency share is similar in Pod D, which had no rise. Higher sick leave is probably an association (viral season) and is not shown to be caused by the alarms. Don't cap agency use or open performance reviews; that would punish the wrong people. Restore the 11 rules, with Clinical Engineering validation and alarm committee sign-off, then track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Don't switch off phone forwarding of alarms. I'm fairly confident, and the remaining unknowns are small: wireless coverage and handset receipt weren't directly tested.
